title: Using Web-based Testing for Large-Scale Assessment

items.abstract: <jats:p>Publicly available web data is increasingly used for applied analysis, yet it is often heterogeneous, weakly structured, and published through technically inconsistent delivery mechanisms. Conventional web scraping and information extraction pipelines typically assume stable HTML structure and predefined schemas, limiting their effectiveness across mixed sources such as official statistical releases, organizational websites, and document-packaged announcements. This paper presents an applied, LLM-assisted multi-mode web scraping and information extraction pipeline designed for non-ideal public web sources, executed through an agentic workflow system (OpenClaw) running on local infrastructure. The contribution is methodological: we formalize distinct extraction modes and fallback strategies-including DOM parsing, browser-rendered extraction, and document-centric parsing-and specify bounded roles for large language models in schema inference, contextual disambiguation, and normalization. Using four empirical case studies drawn from Philippine public data sources, we document extraction outcomes, failure taxonomies, human-in-the-loop validation requirements, and operational tradeoffs affecting feasibility, cost, and reproducibility. The cases span the full spectrum of LLM invocation intensity: from zero LLM involvement (a 41,984-record census-to-boundary crosswalk resolved entirely by deterministic normalization) and Playwright-only rendered extraction of government school directories, through ambiguity-gated LLM cleanup on 12.9%&nbsp;<span>of records (2,039 structured outputs at US$0.27 total LLM cost, 92.5% extracted deterministically), to pervasive LLM involvement across twelve extraction point types in a multi-source startup ecosystem database combining&nbsp;</span><span>static, rendered, and screenshot OCR modes. Concrete cost, coverage, and&nbsp;</span><span>failure-mode data are reported across all four cases, with mid-run operational&nbsp;</span><span>interventions—parser patching, model switching, and checkpoint recovery—</span><span>documented as first-class pipeline events informing reproducibility practice.</span></jats:p>
title: An LLM-Assisted Multi-Mode Web Scraping and Information Extraction Pipeline for Heterogeneous Public Web Data
